spotlights.title: Smart India Hackathon Grand Finale Winners (Software Edition)
spotlights.recipients: Team KernelForge — Rohan Deshmukh (22CSE104), Arjun Nair (23CSE056)
spotlights.description: Awarded First Prize nationally for building a real-time offline-capable rural telemetry diagnostic platform under 36 hours of continuous evaluation.

hackathons.organizer: Ministry of Education Innovation Cell · IIT Madras Nodal Center
hackathons.teamAndRole: Team KernelForge (6 Members) · Lead Backend Architect
hackathons.overallExperience: Over 36 hours with three rounds of jury mentoring, our initial monolithic API hit severe sync bottlenecks on intermittent 2G network simulations. Mentoring feedback at midnight pushed us to redesign around delta-compressed local queues. Presenting the live fault-recovery demo to the industry panel was the most defining engineering experience of our undergraduate journey.

hackathons.organizer: Indian Institute of Science (IISc) Open Systems Track
hackathons.teamAndRole: Team ZeroLatency (4 Members) · Full-Stack & ML Pipeline Lead
hackathons.technologies: Python, FastAPI, ONNX Runtime, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
hackathons.overallExperience: We built an on-device academic plagiarism and citation verifier capable of indexing 10,000+ department PDFs in under 4 seconds using quantized embeddings. Collaborating under tight memory budgets taught us profiling discipline and clean team task handoffs.

interviews.skillsNeeded: Data Structures, Concurrent Systems, OOP Design, Java / C++, Clean Code
interviews.overallExperience: The hiring process consisted of 1 Online Assessment followed by 3 Technical rounds and 1 Values interview. The interviewers cared deeply about writing clean, modular code with exception handling and discussing multiple trade-offs for distributed caching and rate-limiting.

rounds.questionsAsked: Question 1: Multi-source BFS on a grid with obstacle constraints. Question 2: Segment tree range update query problem with modulo arithmetic.
Design an in-memory TTL cache with O(1) get/set and concurrent thread-safe eviction. Asked to write clean Java/C++ code with mutexes.
Design a distributed rate-limiter service (Token Bucket vs Sliding Window Log). Deep dive into my college LabGrid autograder project architecture.

rounds.topicsCovered: Teamwork, Conflict Resolution, "Open Company, No Bullshit"
rounds.questionsAsked: Scenario questions on handling deadline mismatches and how I resolved a major merge conflict during our SIH hackathon sprint.

interviews.keyPreparationTips: Focus heavily on OOP design patterns, concurrency in Java/C++/Go, and explaining your thought process out loud before typing code. Striver SDE sheet and NeetCode 150 were invaluable.
interviews.resourcesUsed: NeetCode 150, Designing Data-Intensive Applications, LeetCode Medium/Hard

interviews.companyDomain: Global Systems, Search & Distributed Cloud Infrastructure
interviews.skillsNeeded: Advanced Graph Algorithms, Dynamic Programming, Trie, Complexity Proofs, C++ / Python
interviews.overallExperience: Cleared 4 back-to-back virtual onsite rounds after passing the Google Kickstart / Online Screening. The emphasis was purely on algorithms, optimal graph traversals, and rigorous time & space complexity proofs.

rounds.questionsAsked: Dependency resolution system with version pinning and cycle detection under resource contention in O(V + E).
Traveling salesman variation with mandatory checkpoints and battery recharging stations.
Real-time autocomplete engine for search queries with top-K frequency ranking in O(K log N).
How do you handle ambiguous project specifications when team members hold conflicting technical opinions?

interviews.keyPreparationTips: Write production-ready code with edge case checks (null inputs, empty arrays, integer overflows). Practice writing code without IDE autocomplete in Google Docs.
interviews.resourcesUsed: CSES Problem Set, LeetCode Hard Graphs, CLRS Algorithms

interviews.skillsNeeded: C Programming, Memory Allocation, Custom Data Structures, Object-Oriented Design
interviews.overallExperience: Classic Zoho recruitment drive: paper-pencil written programming round, basic C logic, advanced DSA implementation without built-in library functions, and low-level application design.

rounds.questionsAsked: Pointer arithmetic output prediction, matrix spiraling, and pattern generation questions.
Implement string substring matching without std::string functions; Evaluate postfix expressions.

rounds.roundTitle: Round 3: Advanced Programming (Design App from Scratch)
rounds.questionsAsked: Build a railway reservation system with waiting list allocation, berth preferences, and ticket cancellation logic in 2 hours.

rounds.topicsCovered: Work culture, willingness to work on proprietary Zoho stacks
rounds.questionsAsked: Discussion on why Zoho, projects completed, and adaptability to in-house frameworks.

interviews.keyPreparationTips: Do not rely heavily on STL / built-in methods. Practice implementing custom stacks, queues, and linked lists from scratch in C++ or Java.
interviews.resourcesUsed: GeeksforGeeks Zoho Archives, OOP principles in Java

interviews.skillsNeeded: Binary Trees, Dynamic Programming, System Design, Operating Systems, C# / C++
interviews.overallExperience: Three rounds focusing heavily on binary tree traversals, memory leak detection, virtual memory, and scalable REST API design.

rounds.questionsAsked: 3 Coding questions in 75 mins: Min deletions to make character frequencies unique, max binary tree path sum variation.
Lowest common ancestor in a binary tree with parent pointers, process vs thread memory spaces.
Design a document collaboration system with undo/redo capabilities and conflict resolution.

interviews.keyPreparationTips: Practice tree traversals and explain OS memory management, virtual memory paging, and multithreading thoroughly.
interviews.resourcesUsed: LeetCode Microsoft tagged, Operating Systems Three Easy Pieces

problems.title: Automated Lab Attendance & Workstation Seat Mapping Sync Issue
problems.description: During 60-student compiler design lab sessions in Lab-3, subnet DHCP lease renewals cause duplicate IP entries in the attendance check-in utility. Looking for someone experienced in MAC-binding or token-based local LAN verification to help patch the check-in service.
